text.p: These are some of the leading stories in Israeli newspapers on Sunday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Palestinian Authority and Israel resume talks in Cairo.
- Israel revokes VIP pass of senior Palestinian officer Tawfik Tirawi.
- European Union peace envoy Miguel Angel Moratinos says Egypt has two weeks to break stalemate.
- Missing family on way to wedding dies in car crash.
- Education Ministry plans to investigate use of dictionaries during English exams.

- Israel and Palestinian Authority will resume negotiations in Cairo today. Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu denies reports by Palestinian and Egyptian sources he will agree to freeze construction of Har Homa settlement.
- Housing Ministry considers uniting two settlements on either side of the Green Line next to Modiin.
- Couple for whom fatal car accident prevented marriage had as it happened met at a car accident in which he was involved and for which she was a witness.

- Cairo meeting to seek formula to renew negotiations. Political sources: It could be a formula by which no houses will be built soon on Har Homa while infrastructure construction continued at the settlement site.
- Prime minister: I didn't promise to freeze settlement construction.
